sec.title: Key points
sec.p: We recommend treatment with an ACE inhibitor or ARB in adults with diabetes and a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 30 mg/g or higher (1B).

sec.title: Background
sec.p: Chronic kidney disease affects approximately 10% of adults worldwide. Smith et al. reported a prevalence of 13.4% in a cohort of 12,000 partici- pants. Further research is needed to clarify progression in younger adults.

sec.title: Methods
sec.p: We searched MEDLINE and Embase from inception to March 2025. Two reviewers independently screened titles and assessed risk of bias.

sec.title: Recommendations for pharmacological management

boxed-text.label: Recommendation 3.1
boxed-text.p: We recommend treatment with an ACE inhibitor or ARB in adults with diabetes and a urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio of 30 mg/g or higher (1B). Serum potassium and creatinine should be checked within 14 days of starting therapy. See Section 4.2 for monitoring intervals.

sec.p: The evidence supporting this recommendation was drawn from four randomised trials with a combined enrolment of 8,412 patients.

boxed-text.label: Recommendation 3.2
boxed-text.p: In patients with advanced disease, the choice of renal replacement therapy should be discussed in a multidisciplinary team meeting after an adequate trial of conservative management (2D).

sec.title: Monitoring intervals
sec.p: Measure eGFR and ACR at least annually in all patients with chronic kidney disease.

list-item.p: Offer a repeat eGFR within 14 days after starting an ACE inhibitor.
Do not offer routine bicarbonate testing in the absence of acidosis.
